::: {.hero-banner}
MLPerf EDU brings industry-standard ML benchmarking to teaching and research.
It preserves the parts of MLPerf methodology that make results trustworthy
(workloads, scenarios, quality targets, measurement discipline, provenance,
reviewable artifacts) while removing the operational friction that keeps most
academic groups from running the official suite. Every core teaching model is
a white-box PyTorch module you can read; every run produces a report you can
hand to a reviewer.
:::

## Two Commands to a First Result

```bash
uv tool install mlperf-edu
mlperf init --profile min
```

The `min` profile runs one representative workload from every suite in under a
minute on a laptop, writing JSON, HTML, and CSV reports plus a `.provd`
provenance artifact for each. From there, `--profile max` runs the full
comparable suite and `--profile pro` opens the research envelope. The
[getting started guide](getting-started.qmd) walks the complete path.

## Why It Exists

Official MLPerf is the enterprise gold standard, but it is difficult for a
classroom or a research group to run, modify, and cite. MLPerf EDU follows the
SPEC playbook instead. It aims to be the benchmark substrate an ML systems
paper reaches for by default, with classroom usability as the forcing function
that keeps it simple enough for students, reviewers, and artifact evaluators.
The [about page](about.qmd) covers the design philosophy and the MLCommons
alignment path.
